page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for standard compute and memory workloads. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, providing 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core across 2 hardware threads. The system includes 8.0 GB of memory, equating to a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 55 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates basic instruction extensions such as AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, but lacks support for advanced vector sets like AVX-512 or AMX accelerators. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero onboard GPUs, requiring external persistent disks for storage needs.

Benchmark results place the processing and memory subsystems predominantly in lower performance tiers relative to broader cloud hardware. Compute evaluations show weak to poor performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1103.39 (bottom 25%) and a multi-core score of 1451.58 (bottom 10%). Geekbench testing mirrors this trend, registering 867.0 in single-core and 1025.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside 1288.0 in Clang software compilation. PassMark scores report an overall CPU score of 3042.75 and an extended instructions score of 1722.27. Memory throughput reaches 79.92 GB/sec for small cached blocks but drops to 11.77 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 10.27 GB/sec for uncached writes, yielding a PassMark memory score of 918.34.

Application and synthetic workload tests further define the operational envelope. Static web serving throughput reaches 1.45 GB/sec, while in-memory Redis SET operations achieve 1.35 million operations per second. PassMark database operations register at 826.31. For lightweight machine learning inference using a 135M parameter model, the server sustains 151.83 prompt tokens per second and 64.91 generation tokens per second. Given the limited single-core throughput and constrained multi-core capacity, this hardware configuration trades high peak compute performance for cost efficiency in resource-constrained, non-critical environments. The server is suited for lightweight web serving, development environments, small background jobs, microservices, and modest testing setups that do not demand high instruction throughput or dedicated local disk I/O.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM built on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.2 GHz. The instance provisions 2 threads across a single physical core, offering 4.0 GB of memory per core alongside 55 MB of L3 cache. It includes no integrated local storage or GPU hardware. In synthetic and application benchmarks, performance ranks primarily in the lower brackets, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1025.0, a PassMark CPU score of 3042.75, uncached memory read bandwidth of 11.77 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput of 1.35 million operations per second. The server trades intensive computing capabilities for balanced entry-level capacity, making it appropriate for lightweight web serving, microservices, small databases, and general dev-test environments.
